assertions.subject: Ulnar Neuropathy
assertions.quote: Ulnar neuropathy at the wrist and hand may manifest as purely sensory, purely motor, or mixed deficits

assertions.subject: Ulnar Neuropathy
assertions.predicate: compression of the deep palmar branch
assertions.quote: The most common presentation involves compression of the deep palmar branch

assertions.subject: Type I lesions
assertions.quote: Type I lesions occur just proximal to or within the Guyon canal, affecting both deep and superficial branches, producing mixed motor and sensory deficits

assertions.subject: Type II lesions
assertions.quote: Type II lesions involve the deep branch exclusively, causing a pure motor deficit

assertions.subject: Type III lesions
assertions.quote: Type III lesions are limited to the superficial branch, resulting in purely sensory deficits

assertions.subject: Ulnar Neuropathy
assertions.quote: Sensory loss in Type I and Type III lesions spares the dorsal hand and fingers and the hypothenar eminence

assertions.subject: Ulnar Neuropathy
assertions.quote: Diagnosis of ulnar neuropathy traditionally depends on clinical history, physical examination, and electrodiagnostic studies

assertions.subject: Ulnar Neuropathy
assertions.quote: the ulnar nerve cross-sectional area at various locations around the elbow rarely exceeds 10 mm
